limits: Single-view image projections describe movement; they do not establish tissue state, muscle activity, joint loading, diagnosis or treatment. Numerical angles depend on camera geometry and tracking. No normative bands are supplied.
gateRole: App display choices: a 5 degree or 0.01 image-unit excursion identifies reportable curve features; three tracked cycles and 70% agreement support repetition wording. These are not validated clinical cutoffs or measurement-error bounds, and never set cycle eligibility or phase boundaries.

regions.title: Ankle / foot
regions.meaning: The foot–shank relationship changes as the body progresses over the foot and the limb prepares for clearance.
regions.limit: Raw projected angle; zero is not neutral dorsiflexion. It does not measure subtalar pronation or supination.
regions.followUp: Review heel and forefoot contact at the marked events; check whether shoes or occlusion alter the toe landmark.

regions.title: Knee
regions.meaning: Knee bending contributes to weight acceptance in loading response and shortens the limb during swing.
regions.limit: Projected knee bend is not a measurement of shock absorption, muscle strength or joint force.
regions.followUp: Review the phase video alongside foot clearance and compare the same phase on the other side.

phaseMeanings.loading_response: Knee bending during weight acceptance contributes to accommodating the incoming load; the angle alone does not measure shock absorption.
phaseMeanings.initial_swing: Knee bending shortens the swinging limb and contributes to space for the foot to pass the ground.
phaseMeanings.midswing: Knee extension advances the lower leg while the foot must remain clear of the ground.
phaseMeanings.terminal_swing: Knee extension positions the limb for the next contact; the video does not measure muscular deceleration.

regions.title: Hip / thigh
regions.meaning: The thigh changes position relative to the trunk during stance progression and forward limb advancement.
regions.limit: This unsigned projection cannot distinguish hip flexion from extension; it is not a clinical hip angle.
regions.followUp: Review thigh position relative to the pelvis at contact and late stance; keep camera direction consistent.

regions.title: Pelvis
regions.meaning: Pelvic movement provides context for support transfer and body progression through the cycle.
regions.limit: Side-view horizontal position is progression, not lateral sway. Front/back hip-line tilt is an image projection, not a Trendelenburg diagnosis.
regions.followUp: Use a level front or back recording to review pelvic levelness during single-limb support.

regions.title: Upper body
regions.frontalAxis: Trunk lean from vertical, image right + (°)
regions.meaning: Upper-body position provides context for how the person progresses and transfers support between the legs.
regions.limit: These projections do not establish balance capacity, compensation or muscle weakness. Frontal displacement follows image left/right.
regions.followUp: Review trunk and pelvis together during each side’s support phase with a fixed, level camera.

phaseGuides.purpose: Prepare the limb for first ground contact.

side: Review whether heel, midfoot or forefoot contacts first.
Review knee posture and trunk position at the marked contact.
front: Review trunk position and visible pelvic level at contact.
back: Review trunk position and visible pelvic level at contact.

context.knee: Knee posture at contact describes how the limb is positioned for weight acceptance.
context.ankle: Foot-contact pattern requires visual review of which part touches first; the raw included angle does not identify it.
context.hip: Thigh position helps describe preparation for contact; this unsigned bend does not distinguish hip flexion from extension.
context.pelvis: A frontal hip-line projection can describe levelness at contact; side-view travel does not measure pelvic drop.
context.trunk: Upper-body position at contact describes the posture entering weight acceptance.

phaseGuides.purpose: Accept support on the newly grounded leg until the opposite foot leaves the ground.

side: Review the transition toward foot-flat without assuming a heel-first strike.
Review knee bending while the foot accepts contact.
front: Review pelvic and trunk movement during transfer onto this limb.
back: Review pelvic and trunk movement during transfer onto this limb.

context.knee: Knee bending during weight acceptance contributes to accommodating the incoming load. Limited visible change alone does not establish poor shock attenuation.
context.ankle: The foot transitions through early contact; heel-to-flat progression applies only when the heel contacts first. The included angle is not calibrated plantarflexion.
context.hip: Thigh–trunk positioning provides context for weight acceptance, without establishing hip stability or muscle activity.
context.pelvis: Frontal pelvic movement describes support transfer; it does not identify hip weakness.
context.trunk: Upper-body movement during weight acceptance can be reviewed alongside knee and foot motion in the same frames.

phaseGuides.purpose: Progress over the supporting foot during single-limb support.

side: Review knee straightening and the body passing over the foot.
Review pelvis-over-ankle alignment as a geometric cue, separately from heel-rise timing.
front: Review pelvic levelness and trunk lean together during this limb’s single support.
back: Review pelvic levelness and trunk lean together during this limb’s single support.

context.knee: Knee straightening contributes to stance progression; its timing should be read within this person’s marked support events.
context.ankle: Shank progression over the foot is relevant to stance rollover; this raw included angle does not establish clinical dorsiflexion.
context.hip: The thigh changes position relative to the trunk as the person progresses over the foot. Signed hip extension is unavailable from this metric.
context.pelvis: Frontal hip-line movement can describe visible pelvic levelness during single support; it is not a Trendelenburg test or a diagnosis.
context.trunk: Trunk position during single support can be compared with the pelvis at the same timestamps; tilt alone does not establish a compensatory cause.

phaseGuides.purpose: Progress beyond the supporting foot before opposite-foot contact.

side: Review heel rise while the forefoot remains in contact.
Review the trailing thigh position relative to the pelvis.
front: Review trunk and pelvis positioning as the opposite foot approaches contact.
back: Review trunk and pelvis positioning as the opposite foot approaches contact.

context.knee: Knee posture contributes to the trailing-limb configuration during late stance.
context.ankle: Heel rise and forefoot contact need visual confirmation; an ankle curve does not measure push-off force.
context.hip: Trailing thigh position is relevant to late stance. The unsigned trunk–thigh angle cannot quantify peak hip extension.
context.pelvis: Pelvic progression provides late-stance context; horizontal side-view travel is not lateral instability.
context.trunk: Upper-body orientation during late stance can be inspected with the heel-rise and opposite-contact frames; it does not measure center-of-mass control.

phaseGuides.purpose: Transition support to the other limb and prepare this foot to leave the ground.

side: Review knee bending as the trailing limb prepares to swing.
Review forefoot contact and the final ground-departure frame.
front: Review visible transfer between limbs around opposite contact and foot departure.
back: Review visible transfer between limbs around opposite contact and foot departure.

context.knee: Knee bending prepares the limb to shorten for swing. Its curve does not measure the speed of weight transfer or unloading force.
context.ankle: Foot orientation changes before departure; the raw ankle angle does not quantify plantarflexion or propulsive force.
context.hip: Thigh movement provides context for the transition into swing without identifying an active muscular drive.
context.pelvis: Pelvic movement can describe the visible support transition, without measuring how much weight each limb carries.
context.trunk: Upper-body orientation can be reviewed across the transfer events; hesitation or unloading cannot be inferred from an isolated angle.

phaseGuides.purpose: Advance the limb after foot departure until the ankles pass each other.

side: Review knee bending and the timing of its swing peak.
Review whether the foot visibly clears the ground.
front: Review hip hiking, outward swing or stance-leg rise as visible movement descriptors.
back: Review hip hiking, outward swing or stance-leg rise as visible movement descriptors.

context.knee: Knee bending shortens the swinging limb and contributes to space for the foot to pass the ground. The peak may occur in a different marked phase in this recording.
context.ankle: The foot–shank relationship contributes to foot positioning, but this included angle and toe image y do not establish calibrated dorsiflexion or ground clearance.
context.hip: Thigh advancement contributes to swing progression; unsigned bend does not establish hip flexor activation or acceleration.
context.pelvis: A frontal view can support review of hip hiking during swing; side-view progression cannot establish it.
context.trunk: Upper-body movement is described during this swing interval. Review those same swing frames before proposing any relationship to limb advancement.

phaseGuides.purpose: Advance the swinging limb from feet adjacent until the shin reaches vertical.

side: Review knee straightening and the shin reaching vertical.
Review the foot–ground relationship directly in the video.
front: Review lateral limb path and visible pelvic movement during swing.
back: Review lateral limb path and visible pelvic movement during swing.

context.knee: Knee extension advances the lower leg while the foot needs room to pass the ground.
context.ankle: Foot orientation during midswing is relevant to clearance review. The current metric does not establish neutral dorsiflexion or diagnose foot drop.
context.hip: The thigh continues its swing positioning; the unsigned angle cannot separate flexion from extension.
context.pelvis: Frontal pelvic movement provides context for the swinging limb’s path; it does not identify the cause of a clearance concern.
context.trunk: Trunk movement during this swing interval can be reviewed alongside the visible foot and limb path.

phaseGuides.purpose: Position the limb for its next ground contact after the shin reaches vertical.

side: Review knee straightening toward the next contact.
Review foot presentation and forward foot reach in the final swing frames.
front: Review visible forward reach and trunk position before contact; perspective limits step-length comparison.
back: Review visible forward reach and trunk position before contact; perspective limits step-length comparison.

context.knee: Knee extension prepares the limb for the next contact; the video does not measure hamstring activity or eccentric deceleration.
context.ankle: Foot presentation before contact needs visual review. The included angle does not establish neutral dorsiflexion or require a heel-first contact.
context.hip: Thigh position contributes to preparation for contact; signed hip flexion and extension remain unavailable from this projection.
context.pelvis: Pelvic position provides context for approach to the next contact; image position alone is not physical step length.
context.trunk: Trunk orientation immediately before contact describes the posture entering the next cycle.

headlineExcluded.reason: Horizontal image progression alone is routine context, not a client finding.

reportPolicy.shapeDefinitions: Interior extrema require a display-sized excursion from both phase endpoints. Plateau extrema are described as the first and last tracked occurrence; no precise physiological peak is inferred. No continuous monotonicity is assumed.
reportPolicy.referenceBoundary: Approximate percentages and 3D reference angles are educational context only, never personal phase timing, angle thresholds or automatic diagnoses.
reportPolicy.phaseBoundaryBoundary: Initial contact is an instant. Heel excursion is a provisional contact proxy; pelvis-over-ankle alignment is distinct from the current heel-rise phase boundary.
reportPolicy.mixedShapes: Equal-frequency cycle shapes are labelled mixed, never an arbitrary dominant pattern. Small ambiguous reversals without a net or prominent interior feature remain chart detail rather than client headlines.
